answer: A 100 ms trigger does not give real-time latency. Each micro-batch cycle pays a fixed overhead of about 1 second for planning and committing offsets, so a 100 ms trigger spends almost all its time on that overhead, and the batch model stops paying below about 1 second. Shrinking the trigger also cannot fix tail latency: p99 is roughly the trigger plus the slowest run. If the SLA is sub-second (e.g., 300 ms), no trigger fits and a record-at-a-time engine is needed. If the SLA is seconds or minutes, micro-batch on the existing cluster may suffice, so match the trigger to the SLA first.
